routes.name: Citizens of the United States, Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia

note: Marshall Islands, read in the Immigration Regulations of 2009 as the Judiciary publishes them (rmicourts.org, 2026-11-03), the only immigration regulations on its list of selected regulations, which names amended versions where there are any. Everyone but the exempt must have a visa approved before arriving (applied for abroad); citizens of the United States, Palau and the Federated States of Micronesia need none, and the Labor (Non-Resident Workers) Act exempts them from the work permit too (so they may work at anything, the work engine's reading). A work visa lasts up to two years, or less to match the work permit, and is issued only to someone already holding a work permit; the Immigration Act entitles the employer granted the permit to a work visa for that employee, read as work for the sponsor. A temporary work visa lasts up to six months on a letter from the Labor Division and can't be renewed or extended; how far it ties the holder to an employer isn't said, so it's left out. A business visa needs a foreign investment business licence and a work permit; the work it allows beyond the business isn't stated. Every other visa here may be renewed to the Act's maximum. The general visa (a spouse or dependent child; no business) has no fee in Schedule 1, so none is kept; the student and dependent adult visas allow no employment. Fees are paid to the Ministry of Finance in US dollars. Not modelled: the alien registration card every visa holder staying over six months must also hold ($50, valid to 31 December and renewed each year, $55 if late), the refundable bond the Director may set for a stay over 90 days, the provisional business visa (three months, to seek business), and the work permit itself: the Labor Division's application sheet of 2007 on the same site gives a $100 application fee and 21 days to process, but no later schedule was read, the Nonresident Workers (Fee) Act's fees weren't reached, and the permit is the work engine's, so neither is kept on the visa. The Regulations name no permanent residence, and no naturalisation years are read here. Read again on 2026-11-03: web.archive.org couldn't be read (web.archive.org reset every connection each time it was tried, and PacLII itself answered 403 behind a Cloudflare check), so its reading of 2026-10-31 stands.

sources.title: Republic of the Marshall Islands, Immigration Regulations of 2009 (approved by Cabinet, C.M. 189 (2009), December 2009), as the RMI Judiciary publishes them among its selected regulations
sources.said: §5(1) The following persons shall be exempted from the requirement to hold a visa to enter the Republic: ... (c) a citizen of the United States; (d) a citizen of Palau or the Federated States of Micronesia ... §7 Except as provided under Sections 5 and 6, citizens from all other countries must apply for visa prior to entering the Republic. §10(1) ... (b) Business visas (B-1) shall be valid for a period of up to two (2) years with multiple entries. Business visas shall be issued to a person who has a Foreign Investment Business license (FIBL) and a work permit. ... (d) Work visas (E-1) shall be valid for a period of up to two (2) years, or a lesser period which correspond to the length of work permit, with multiple entries. Before the issuance of Work visa a person must possess a valid work permit. (e) Student visas (S-1) shall be valid for a period of up to twelve (12) months with multiple entries. ... The holder shall not be allowed to seek or to be engaged in any employment and business activities in the Republic. ... (h) General visa (G-1) shall be valid for a period of up to two (2) years with multiple entries. The holder is prohibited to engaged in any business, activities in the Republic. Persons who are eligible for a General Visa: (i) legal spouse; (ii) dependent child. (i) Dependent Adult Visa (DA-1) shall be valid for up to two (2) years with multiple entries. The holder is prohibited to seek or to be engaged in any employment or business activities in the Republic. (j) Temporary work visa (TE-1) shall be valid for a period of up to six (6) months with multiple entries ... §11(1) Visas issued under these Regulations may be renewed or extended to the maximum period allowable under the Act ... (2) The following visas shall not be renewed or extended: (a) visitors visa (V-1) (b) Transit visa (T-1) (c) Cruising Visa (C-1) (d) Temporary Work Visa (TE-1) (e) Provisional Business Visa (B-2). §13(1) Subject to the exemption provisions of the Act, all visa applications must be submitted to the Director of Immigration and the relevant visas must be approved and issued prior to the applicant entering the Republic. §15(1)(d) if applying for a work visa, a letter from the Labor Division indicating that a work permit has been issued; (h) if applying for a temporary work visa, a letter indication duration of the stay and a granted letter from Labor Division. §23(1) Every person issued with a visa who intends to remain in the Republic for a consecutive period of more than six (6) months; must apply for and obtain an alien registration card. ... (3)(c) valid for one year and renewable annually. (4) All alien registration cards shall expire on December 31 every year. Schedule 1, Fees: Application for a business visa USD 300.00 Ministry of Finance; Application for a work visa USD 200.00 Ministry of Finance; Application for a visitor's visa USD 100.00; Application for a student visa USD 150.00; Application for a transit visa USD 50.00; Temporary work visa USD 150.00; ... Adult Dependent $200; ... Alien Registration Card $50.00; Provisional Business Visa $150.

sources.title: Labor Division, Republic of the Marshall Islands, 'Applications for Work Permits' and checklist of supporting documents (2007), as the RMI Judiciary publishes it among its selected regulations as the Work Permit Regulations, 2007
sources.said: 1. Applications for work permits should consist of the following: (i) Completed application form (ii) Supporting documents (refer to requirements below) (iii) Receipt of payment of application fee ($100) 2. Please submit complete applications and supporting documents to the office of the Labor Division, Ministry of Foreign Affairs ... 3. Applications will take 21 days to process. ... OSL Work Permits ... General Work Permits ... Letter of support from employer ... Employment Contract - between employer and employee ... Temporary Work Permits: Letter from employer stating position, purpose and duration ... Family Work Permits ... Foreign Investor Work Permits ... Extension of Work Permits ... Transfer of Work Permits ... Letter of support from original employer ... Employment Contract - between new employer and employee

sources.title: Labor (Non-Resident Workers) Act 2006 (16 MIRC ch. 1), s. 110 (PacLII's consolidated copy, archive.org snapshot of 17 December 2024)
sources.said: Any person who is not a citizen of the Republic is prohibited from undertaking employment in the Republic unless that person is: ... the holder of a work permit granted under this Chapter ; or ... The following persons are exempt from the requirement to hold a work permit: ... a citizen of the United States; ... a citizen of Palau or the Federated States of Micronesia; ... exempted persons are required to comply with registration requirements of the Labor Division

sources.title: Immigration Act 2006 (43 MIRC ch. 1), ss. 113, 136 (PacLII's consolidated copy, archive.org snapshot of 3 March 2016)
sources.said: Every employer that is issued with a work permit under the Labor (Non-Resident Workers) Act 2006 in respect of a non-resident worker, shall, subject to the person’s application being denied under section 114, be entitled to be issued with a work visa in respect of that employee.
